contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers documents private-preview, nonrecurring French meal-voucher cards in EUR, with Elements and partial Connect. A French Stripe account, CNTR approval for each accepting branch, a commercial agreement with at least one supported issuer, and prior provisioning of that branch's SIRET are separate prerequisites (new raw lines 9-23, new raw lines 25-76 and new raw lines 78-101). Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner follow the documented benefit integration and have no dispute resolution system. Swile is a separate Mastercard route with eligibility determined by Swile (old raw lines 69-78 and old raw lines 96-100, new raw lines 80-91 and new raw lines 109-113). The daily balance cap is €25, and the available balance refreshes at midnight French local time (old raw lines 136-140 and new raw lines 150-154). The overview describes per-PaymentIntent opt-in with the provisioned SIRET and saved-card identification from `PaymentMethod.card.benefits`; neither the optional balance check nor creation of an Intent establishes payment (new raw lines 119-154). Issuers settle directly with the acceptor outside Stripe. The negative BalanceTransaction is Stripe's processing fee, separate from issuer fees. Captured payments lack refunds, while a separate manual authorization can be released before capture (new raw lines 103-117). The merchant orchestrates separate payments for ineligible fees or overage (new raw lines 156-160). The May capture establishes the same product flow (old raw lines 65-116 and old raw lines 136-146). source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers.md broadly preserves it but omits the issuer agreement and newly shown waitlist route, and its GET balance verb conflicts with the detailed guides' POST.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers, the November addition is the documented email waitlist request, an access route for the existing private preview (old raw lines 8-10 and new raw lines 9-23). Other edits are presentational and the product semantics, settlement and capture limits remain dated to both captures (old raw lines 80-116 and new raw lines 93-129). source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers.md and the voucher concept need reciprocal scope for the overviews' dated literal SIRET and scalar PaymentMethod example. The separate November purchase, save and Connect routes require preview Stripe version `2026-05-27.preview` or later (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:25-29`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-saving-payment-details-2026-11-07.md:25-29`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-with-connect-2026-11-07.md:38-42`). The preview workflow requires an active location and passes `payment_details[location]` plus the conditional voucher benefit on PaymentIntent, with distinct `setup_details` for SetupIntent and on-session reuse. The separate payment guide resolves the location's stored SIRET at confirmation, without changing already-confirmed payments. The overview estimates 1–3 business days for branch provisioning (old raw lines 86-88 and new raw lines 99-101), while the detailed Dashboard and API guides describe 1–2 business days for their respective onboarding workflows. Dashboard immutability and API acknowledged changes with paused acceptance during re-onboarding apply to their respective routes (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:25-39,58-74`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-saving-payment-details-2026-11-07.md:25-71`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-2026-11-07.md:31-51`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:96-112,192-198,285-310`). Connect's PaymentMethod example is an array while its ConfirmationToken preview remains scalar (new raw lines 131-148; `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-with-connect-2026-11-07.md:74-109`). The balance guide documents POST on a saved PaymentMethod, with an as-of balance that does not reserve funds. The split-tender prose puts the secondary payment first or uses manual capture for the voucher after the secondary payment succeeds. The diagram starts with the voucher PaymentIntent and calls for reversion if the secondary payment fails. The voucher can be released while its authorization remains uncaptured. A captured voucher payment cannot be refunded (old raw lines 96-100 and old raw lines 136-146, new raw lines 109-113 and new raw lines 150-160; `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-checking-a-card-balance-2026-11-07.md:25-60,89-114`). A waitlist request, optional balance check and payment-creation example establish neither preview admission nor actual capture or issuer payout.
